source.section: Form IN-111 Lines 1-8 and 14 (booklet PDF pp.10-11), standard deduction chart and Lines 4-5e (PDF p.11), rate schedules (PDF p.46); age box: 'born before Jan. 2, 1961' (PDF pp.10-11 Line 4)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 1) 50,010.00 + private pension (person 0) 40,000.00 = 90,010.00. Federal taxable income = 90,010.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65 additional = 56,910.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form IN-111, Married Filing Jointly: Line 1 federal AGI 90,010.00. Schedule IN-112 Part I: Line 1 all state and local obligation interest 0.00; Line 2 Vermont obligations 0.00; Line 3 = 0.00; Line 4 0.00; Line 6 total additions 0.00. Subtractions: Lines 7-16c all 0.00; Line 18 total subtractions 0.00. Line 19 net modifications = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00. Form IN-111 Line 2 0.00; Line 3 = 90,010.00 + (0.00) = 90,010.00. Line 4 standard deduction 15,300.00 + 1 x 1,250.00 age box(es) = 16,550.00 [person 0 born 1955-06-15 (65 or older: box checked), person 1 born 1962-03-03 (not born before Jan. 2, 1961: no box)]. Line 5a-5d personal exemptions 2; Line 5e 2 x 5,300.00 = 10,600.00. Line 6 = 16,550.00 + 10,600.00 = 27,150.00. Line 7 Vermont taxable income = 90,010.00 - 27,150.00 = 62,860.00. Line 8: schedule tax on 62,860.00 (Schedule Y-1, booklet p.46, merged continuous schedule): 3.35% x (62,860.00 - 0.00) = 2,105.81; the tax table (pp.47-51) gives 2105. Federal AGI 90,010.00 is not greater than 150,000.00, so no minimum tax: Line 8 2,105.81. Line 9 0.00 (no Schedule IN-119 items; Credit for the Elderly or the Disabled not modelled); Line 10 2,105.81; Lines 11-13 0.00; Line 14 Vermont income tax 2,105.81.
accepted_approximations: The rate schedule is one continuous schedule: the printed rows that restart at 75,000 are merged and printed base taxes, rounded to the dollar, are not used. Below 75,000 the booklet uses tax tables in 100 dollar rows.
